question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 20 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 22 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 14 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(20, 22, 14) = 1540 units

Total combined efficiency = (1540 ÷ 20) + (1540 ÷ 22) + (1540 ÷ 14) = 77 + 70 + 110 = 257 units/hour

Time taken together = Total Work ÷ Total efficiency = 1540 ÷ 257 = 5²⁵⁵⁄₂₅₇ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5²⁵⁵⁄₂₅₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe A = 20 hours

Time taken by pipe B = 22 hours

Time taken by pipe C = 14 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given times

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of pipes A, B and C together = 77 + 70 + 110 = 257 units/hour

⇒ Time required when operating together = Total Work ÷ Total efficiency

⇒ Time required = 1540 ÷ 257

⇒ Time required = 5²⁵⁵⁄₂₅₇ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5²⁵⁵⁄₂₅₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns - Inlet vs Outlet

An inlet pipe fills a tank and its efficiency is considered positive. An outlet pipe empties a tank and its efficiency is taken as negative.

Work & Time Relation

Efficiency and Time are inversely proportional to each other. Total Work = Time taken × Efficiency.

Combined Rate Method

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part of the tank filled by it in 1 hour is 1/x. For multiple pipes working together, simply add their 1-hour work capacities.
